LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the scope of electronics, apply lab safety rules, and identify common electronic components and test equipment.
LectureTopics: Overview of electronics: applications and career opportunities
Laboratory safety rules and handling of electronic equipment
Introduction to common electronic components: resistors, capacitors, diodes, and transistors
Using a digital multimeter: measuring voltage, current, and resistance
AssessmentMethods: Component identification practical and safety rules written quiz
FeedbackComments: Thorough introduction. Ensure all students complete the safety induction form before lab entry.

Topic: Introduction to Wood and Timber Products
LearningOutcomes: Students will classify timber types, describe their properties, and select appropriate timber for given carpentry applications.
LectureTopics: Classification of timber: hardwood vs softwood species
Timber defects: knots, warping, splits, and their effect on structural performance
Timber processing and seasoning methods
Common timber products used in Zambian carpentry and furniture industry
AssessmentMethods: Practical timber sample identification and short written test on timber properties
FeedbackComments: Good use of local timber samples. Consider bringing in samples from Ndola timber yards.

Topic: Motor Vehicle Safety and Workshop Practice
LearningOutcomes: Students will apply automotive workshop safety rules, identify PPE requirements, and demonstrate safe use of basic automotive hand tools.
LectureTopics: Automotive workshop hazards: chemical, mechanical, and fire risks
Personal protective equipment (PPE) in the automotive workshop
Safe use and storage of hand tools and workshop equipment
Vehicle lifting and support procedures using jacks and stands
AssessmentMethods: Practical safety demonstration and tool identification exercise
FeedbackComments: Safety content is comprehensive. Include a practical vehicle lifting demonstration on a workshop vehicle.

LearningOutcomes: Students will identify internal and external computer hardware components, describe their functions, and perform a basic computer assembly task.
LectureTopics: Types of computers: desktop, laptop, server, and embedded systems
Internal components: CPU, RAM, motherboard, power supply, and storage
External peripherals: input devices (keyboard, mouse) and output devices (monitor, printer)
Practical: safe computer disassembly and reassembly

Materials.Title: PC Assembly and Disassembly Reference Notes

AssessmentMethods: Hardware identification quiz and practical PC assembly assessment
FeedbackComments: Well-structured. Ensure sufficient computers are available for the practical session.

LearningOutcomes: Students will interpret electronic schematic diagrams, identify components from circuit symbols, and plan the assembly of a given circuit from a schematic.
LectureTopics: Standard electronic circuit symbols and their physical component counterparts
Reading and interpreting schematic diagrams
Introduction to PCB layouts and their relationship to schematics
Practical: tracing a circuit diagram and identifying components on a sample PCB
AssessmentMethods: Schematic reading practical exercise and component identification from circuit diagrams
